name: Eiffel Tower
_about: THE EIFFEL TOWER, Paris (1887-89): four lattice legs on a 125m square, leaning in on a nearly exponential curve to merge in one shaft; floors at 57.6, 115.7 and 276m; Sauvestre's four arches under the first floor's girders; the lantern at 300m and the mast to 330m. Every iron member is a real bar (`truss`, `bars`: arch/truss.js). Generated by tools/archgen/eiffel_tower.py -- edit the script for arithmetic changes.

feet._about: the masonry pedestal under each leg, 27m square

lower legs._about: one leg's great lattice, turned to its four corners: a square box of four chords, a strut and two crossing diagonals to a face

leg ribs._about: the fine lattice's ribs up each leg's faces, three to a face, so that from afar the leg's great diagonals have a screen of iron behind them

shaft._about: the four legs become one square lattice shaft, thinning to the third floor

lift guides._about: the lift's guides up the shaft's middle

arches._about: Sauvestre's arch, 68m across and to 39.5m, a lattice rib along the tower's outer face: it carries nothing and is the tower's face

spandrels._about: uprights from the arch's back to the girder, and iron rings in the spandrels

first floor girders._about: the great girders that hold the legs together at the first floor, 10m deep, on the outer faces

first floor arcade._about: the arcade of little arches under the first floor's gallery, the band the tower's waist is known by

first floor._about: the first floor, a square ring round its well, 71m across

first floor pavilions._about: the four pavilions of the first floor, between the legs

second floor._about: the second floor, 42m across, the lift's well in its middle

second floor girders._about: its girders, on the outer faces

second floor pavilions._about: the small pavilions of the second floor, between the legs' heads

third floor gallery._about: the glazed gallery all round the third floor

third floor deck._about: the open deck over it, overhanging

crown._about: the crown that carries the lantern over the deck: four ribs curving in as the tower's own edges do, braced

crown room._about: Eiffel's own small room on the deck

lantern deck._about: the lantern's small deck where the ribs meet

mast._about: the mast, to 330m (1889's flagstaff stood to 312m)
